abstract: This IMF Staff Discussion Note examines AI's labor market impact, finding that employment in AI-vulnerable occupations is 3.6% lower in regions with high AI-skill demand after 5 years. The analysis reveals significant geographic divergence driven by skill concentration, with implications for labor market inequality and the need for skills-bridging policies in the AI age.
keyFindings: Employment is 3.6% lower in AI-vulnerable occupations in regions with high AI-skill demand after 5 years.
Geographic divergence in employment outcomes is driven by skill concentration across regions.
Labor market displacement is concentrated in specific occupations susceptible to AI automation.
Regions with pre-existing AI expertise and skills infrastructure experience different employment dynamics than those without.
